title: Segmented retention enforcement for analytics events with scrub-first delete pipeline
creator: Priya Singh
description: Problem: Our current analytics pipeline stores event payloads containing user-identifying fields for longer than necessary in several downstream materialized tables and search indexes. This creates regulatory risk for GDPR/CCPA and increases blast radius for data leaks. Goal: Implement a segmented retention enforcement system that applies per-customer and per-event-class retention and performs scrub-first deletion (redact indexes and materialized views, then asynchronously backfill erase in object store). The solution should provide auditable deletion records and support legal holds and export for compliance teams.
acceptance_criteria: Retention rules can be defined per tenant and per event-type via Console UI and persisted to the retention-policy service
Events older than policy thresholds are either redacted (PII removed) or fully erased depending on policy flags
Audit log entries are emitted for each deletion/redaction action with trace IDs linked to the original ingestion request
Search indexes and analytics materialized tables do not surface PII after a policy run - verified by automated integration tests
Legal hold flag prevents erase but still allows redaction; hold release triggers scheduled erase
Service supports a dry-run mode to simulate deletes and generate reports without modifying data
End-to-end pipelines meet defined SLO: deletion job completes within 48 hours for datasets under 10M events and emits completion metric
updates: 2026-03-02: Scoping session with PM and Compliance. Agreed to model retention at (tenant,event_type) granularity rather than full-tenant only.

2026-03-04: Spike complete - prototype of scrub-first workflow using streaming redactors and a tombstone marker in events-stream table. Found strong contention when backfilling large indices; requires chunked index-update approach.
2026-03-07: Design review with infra: decided to use idempotent 'erase_job' records in the retention service and to drive workers via SQS-style queue to avoid double deletes.
2026-03-10: Compliance requested retention policy schema to include 'reason_code' and 'regulatory_tag' fields to improve auditability. Updated schema draft.
2026-03-12: Implemented API for policy CRUD; backend persists to config-store. Still pending UI surface in Console (PM + Design ticket pending).

2026-03-14: Started integration tests for scrub-first path against staging index. Observed 8% throughput regression on ingestion when running scrub hotpath; need optimization (batching of redact ops).
decision_log: Keep soft-delete marker approach rather than immediate object deletion to allow reversible legal holds and to minimize risk of inconsistent state
Adopt scrub-first order: redact sensitive fields in hot stores (Postgres, materialized views, search) before scheduling irreversible erasure in cold object storage
Use chunked index updates (batch size 5k docs) with backoff to avoid search cluster overload during mass redact runs
Retention policy schema will include: tenant_id, event_type, retention_days, mode(redact|erase|hold), reason_code, regulatory_tag
Audit events will be immutable and written to write-ahead audit stream in Kafka with retention aligned to compliance team needs
testing_plan: Unit tests for retention policy validation and enforcement logic
Integration test: ingest synthetic PII-bearing events -> apply policy -> assert redaction in materialized table and absence in search results
Chaos test: simulate worker restarts and duplicate erase_job deliveries to validate idempotency
Performance test: measure ingestion QPS impact with scruber enabled (target <10% regression), iterate batching settings
Compliance test: generate audit export for a sample tenant and validate completeness against legal checklist
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): Enable for internal tenants only; run full dry-run reports for two weeks
Phase 1 (canary): Turn on scrub-first for 5 low-risk customers; monitor metrics and search cluster load
Phase 2 (gradual): Ramp to 25% of tenants with rolling throttling and alerting; require signoff from Security and Compliance
Phase 3 (global): Default enforcement on for new tenants; existing tenants get migration window and opt-in before forced mode
Rollback: disable policy worker and replay markers to revert to pre-scrub state where possible; ensure audit trail documents rollback reason
